t: Bangkok began as a customs outpost of Ayutthaya on the Chao Phraya River, became King Taksin's capital of Thonburi in 1767, and was refounded on the east bank by Rama I in 1782.
Under Mongkut and Chulalongkorn the city took the steam engine, the printing press, paved roads, railways, electricity and Western-style architecture, and Chinese immigrants led its trade.

In the 20th century Bangkok was the stage of Thailand's political struggles, from the end of absolute monarchy in 1932 to student uprisings and coups, while its population grew from about 50,000 in 1822 to millions.
dyk: Bangkok's full ceremonial name, given in the reign of King Mongkut, is listed in Guinness World Records as the world's longest place name, at 168 letters.

f.founded: It is not known exactly when the area was first settled; a customs outpost under Ayutthaya existed by the 15th century. The city dates its foundation as the capital to 21 April 1782, when King Rama I erected the city pillar on the east bank.
f.where: In the delta of the Chao Phraya River in the central plain of Thailand, about 25 km from the river's mouth on the Gulf of Thailand.
f.known: A customs outpost of Ayutthaya; the siege of 1688 that expelled the French; Thonburi under King Taksin; the Rattanakosin capital of 1782; Siam's modernisation under Mongkut and Chulalongkorn; its Chinese community; canals and floating houses; its place as the nation's political stage
f.today: Bangkok is the capital and largest city of Thailand, governed as a special administrative area by the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration.
